decisions.title: Terminate blocked interactive-fallback tool calls
decisions.rationale: Pi's new terminating block result is a reversible, low-risk way to stop the automatic follow-up model call when ce-workflow rejects work_goal_human_decision because ask_user is available. The existing tool_call guard is the exact shared boundary, so adding terminate removes one unnecessary model turn without changing the decision flow.
decisions.verification: node scripts/test-work-goal.mjs passed and asserts the blocked interactive fallback returns block=true and terminate=true

decisions.title: Provider authentication readiness CLI
decisions.rationale: pi auth check validates provider credential readiness, while ce-workflow's agent health preflight must verify each configured model through the in-process ModelRegistry.complete path, including its actual endpoint and response. Spawning the CLI would add a second runtime-resolution path and still require the current probe; revisit only if Pi exposes a model-level readiness API through the extension context that can replace inference probes without losing coverage.

decisions.title: Host tool-prompt, provider, TUI, theme, and runtime updates
decisions.rationale: Built-in tool prompt contribution exports, Qwen catalog support, fullscreen interaction and rendering fixes, terminal theme probing, Agent.reset safety, and binary startup fixes are host-owned behavior inherited by ce-workflow. This package neither constructs Pi's built-in tool harness nor duplicates those provider and TUI internals, so local adapters would add code without replacing an incumbent path.

decisions.title: Verified private workflow generation
decisions.rationale: The official stable release is translated into the complete private nine-workflow generation with no ordinary CE runtime surface.

decisions.title: Async interrupt safety and workflow completion reliability
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 (baseline-only adoption; easy rollback by package version). Bottom line: adopt 0.45.1’s package-owned async safety and workflow reliability fixes with no ce-workflow source shim. Verified project fit: ce-workflow routes coded roles through `extensions/work-models.js`’s shared async RPC wrapper and relies on status/reconciliation; upstream 0.45.1 prevents interrupts from signaling unverified/shared host PIDs, publishes result data before terminal status, and drops late child responses after workflow settlement. Benefit: safer async control and fewer completion races/duplicates. Cost/risk: low package regression risk; no local code change. Confidence: high. Recommendation: Adopt now.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-subagents version is 0.45.1 and node scripts/test-work-start-finish.mjs passed against the shared RPC wrapper

decisions.title: Structured wait completions, live activity, and caller guidance
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1. Bottom line: add no ce-workflow adapter for structured `subagent_wait` completions, live workflow activity, Markdown-fence diagnostics, Herdr command quoting, configured reads, or clarified mission policy. Verified project fit: current direct-role status and transcript reconciliation already covers required telemetry, the shared RPC wrapper safely serializes task text with JSON.stringify, and ce-workflow deliberately keeps `mission:false`; no current correctness gap or removable local code was found. Benefit: avoids duplicating canonical upstream status and UI behavior. Cost/risk: exact wait-only artifact identity remains unused, but can be revisited if a measured telemetry gap appears. Confidence: high. Recommendation: inherit the package behavior without local code.

decisions.title: Responsive decision UI and Herdr attention signaling
decisions.rationale: Responsive list layouts and blocked/waiting attention signals are implemented inside pi-ask-user and inherited by ce-workflow's existing ask_user calls. Local dialog policy remains separate and no compatibility shim is required.

decisions.title: ask_user telemetry integration
decisions.rationale: The release exposes no stable per-call telemetry API, while ce-workflow already records tool timing and dialog decisions. Local wrapping would duplicate package behavior without measurable savings; revisit if a public metrics hook appears.

decisions.title: Connected-target safety and broker routing reliability
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 (baseline-only adoption; easy package rollback). Bottom line: adopt 0.10.0’s package-owned routing and reliability improvements with no ce-workflow source change. Verified project fit: ce-workflow treats pi-intercom as optional and uses only public `contact_supervisor`/`intercom` actions plus exact-session, pending-ask, and explicit-reply safeguards. Upstream 0.10.0 hardens reconnect/mailbox identity, refuses blocking asks to disconnected targets, validates broker payloads, and adds cwd-scoped visible project panes without changing required existing calls. Benefit: safer stale/disconnected coordination and inherited broker reliability. Cost/risk: low package regression risk; project panes and extension-bus state remain unused. Confidence: high. Recommendation: Adopt now.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-intercom version is 0.10.0 and node scripts/test-work-goal.mjs passed the exact-session, pending-ask, and explicit-reply policy assertions

decisions.title: Implicit replies, project panes, and extension-bus state
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1. Bottom line: retain ce-workflow’s explicit `pending` plus `reply` coordination rule and add no project-pane or extension-bus integration. Verified project fit: exact reply threading is a deliberate stale-message safety boundary, bounded cross-codebase work already uses pi-subagents with explicit cwd, and ce-workflow has no shared-state consumer that would justify a second cross-session store. Benefit: preserves thread identity and avoids new Herdr/state coupling. Cost/risk: ce-workflow does not use the release’s convenience surfaces, while ordinary direct users still can. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local action.

decisions.title: Recover abandoned native-compaction fences
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 (small guard plus one focused regression). Bottom line: release ce-workflow’s native-compaction single-flight fence when a new turn begins without the expected `session_compact` event. Verified project fit: `extensions/work-models.js` marks native compaction in flight during `session_before_compact`; previously only `session_compact`/explicit reset cleared it, so an abandoned host compaction could leave F8 microcompaction permanently reporting “already in progress.” The reviewed pi-goal 0.49.7 lifecycle avoids treating `session_before_compact` as proof of completion and schedules continuation only after compact/settled boundaries. Benefit: prevents a stuck autonomous-goal compaction fence. Cost/risk: low; the guard only clears native-owned state at an actual new-turn boundary and leaves ce-workflow-owned compaction untouched. Confidence: high. Recommendation: Adopt now.
decisions.verification: node scripts/test-work-goal.mjs passed and covers native fence retention before turn_start plus recovery on the next turn

decisions.title: Replace ce-workflow autonomous goals with pi-goal managed runs
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2; confidence: high. pi-goal 0.49.7's default-off managed-run RPC, response/no-progress limits, queue, tools, TUI, and settled continuation lifecycle are well-defined, but replacing ce-workflow's engine would add an optional package dependency while losing self-improving mode, work-item-aware completion gates, guided ask_user decisions, context microcompaction, usage-limit retry, and ce-workflow telemetry. The RPC cannot delete the incumbent path without a parallel compatibility layer, so retain the project-owned engine and reuse only the concrete lifecycle fix above.

decisions.title: Checkpoint trust, resumable graphs, and diagnostic quality
decisions.rationale: Checkpoint-bounded secret scanning, trusted cold-start graph resume, stricter structural scans, improved LSP diagnostics, confidence labels, and duplicate suppression directly improve tools ce-workflow already invokes. They are package-owned and require no local adapter.

decisions.title: Standalone build-graph command for verifier cold starts
decisions.rationale: ce-workflow's verifier intentionally falls back when a review graph is cold rather than initiating a workspace-wide build from a read-only checkpoint. Calling build-graph would add latency and trust-scope complexity without improving required correctness; revisit only if measured cold-cache misses materially reduce verifier value.

decisions.title: Prompt-cache and scanner observability surfaces
decisions.rationale: Machine-global cache metrics, CLI output, language coverage, and scanner rule maintenance are pi-lens operational surfaces. ce-workflow consumes bounded diagnostics and has no stable local API or abstraction to replace.
